name: Taj Mahal
summary: Ivory-white marble mausoleum in Agra, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
history: The Taj Mahal was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Construction began around 1632. The main mausoleum was completed around 1648, while additional elements of the complex were completed by 1653. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
architecture: A masterpiece of Mughal architecture combining Persian, Islamic and Indian influences. The complex features a white-marble mausoleum on a raised platform, four minarets, a central dome, symmetrical Mughal gardens, decorative stone inlay, and red-sandstone mosque and guest-house structures.

name: Agra Fort
summary: The walled imperial city of the Mughals in Agra, rebuilt in red sandstone by Emperor Akbar from 1565 and later embellished in white marble by Shah Jahan.
history: The official Agra district tourism page describes Agra Fort as the walled imperial city of the Mughals and states that Emperor Akbar rebuilt it in red sandstone from 1565, with later white-marble additions by Shah Jahan.
architecture: The fort's 2.5-kilometre ramparts enclose structures including Jahangir Mahal, Khas Mahal, Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Sheesh Mahal, Musamman Burj and Moti Masjid.

sources.title: Agra District Administration: Agra Fort

name: Fatehpur Sikri
summary: Historic red-sandstone city in Agra district founded by Emperor Akbar in 1571 and used as the Mughal capital for about 14 years.
history: The official Agra district tourism page states that Akbar founded Fatehpur Sikri in 1571 and that it served as the Mughal capital for about 14 years.
architecture: The complex includes Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, the marble Tomb of Sheikh Salim Chishti, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas and Jodha Bai's Palace. The district page describes a blend of Persian, Hindu and Jain architectural idioms.

sources.title: Agra District Administration: Fatehpur Sikri

name: Akbar's Tomb (Sikandra)
summary: Mausoleum of the Mughal emperor Akbar, located in Sikandra near Agra.
history: The official Agra district tourism page says the mausoleum was begun by Akbar and completed by his son Jahangir in 1613. It stands in a 119-acre charbagh at Sikandra.
architecture: The five-storeyed sandstone-and-marble pyramid and its gateway combine Hindu, Islamic and Persian motifs, according to the official Agra district tourism page.

name: Mehtab Bagh
summary: Mughal charbagh garden across the Yamuna River from the Taj Mahal, laid out originally by Babur and later aligned by Shah Jahan.
history: The official Agra district tourism page describes Mehtab Bagh as originally laid out by Babur and later aligned by Shah Jahan with the Taj Mahal across the Yamuna.
architecture: The restored charbagh includes fruit trees and pathways, according to the official Agra district tourism page.

sources.title: Agra District Administration: Mehtab Bagh

name: Ram Bagh (Aram Bagh)
summary: Ram Bagh, also known as Bagh-i-Gul Afshan, is a Mughal garden laid out by Emperor Babur around 1528 and regarded as the oldest surviving Mughal garden in India.
history: The Agra District Administration describes Ram Bagh as laid out by Emperor Babur around 1528 and as the oldest surviving Mughal garden in India.
architecture: The garden has terraced walkways, water channels and pavilions overlooking the Yamuna, and is described by the Agra District Administration as a prototype of the charbagh tradition.

sources.title: Ram Bagh (Bagh-i-Gul Afshan) - Agra District Administration

name: Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah
summary: Mughal-era riverside tomb commissioned by Empress Nur Jahan for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg; often called the Baby Taj.
history: The tomb was commissioned by Empress Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg and was built between 1622 and 1628, according to official Agra tourism information.

architecture: A compact Mughal tomb notable for extensive marble decoration and inlay work, with a garden setting beside the Yamuna River.

name: Chini ka Rauza
summary: Mughal-period tomb associated with Afzal Khan, a Persian poet and high-ranking official under Shah Jahan, near the Yamuna.
history: Official tourism information identifies Chini ka Rauza as the tomb of Allama Afzal Khan, also known as Mullah Shukrullah Shirazi, a poet-scholar and prime minister to Shah Jahan.

sources.title: Agra District Administration: Historic Tourist Places

history: The official Agra district tourism listing identifies the monument as the tomb of Mariam-uz-Zamani and places it near Akbar's Tomb at Sikandra.

name: Jama Masjid, Agra
summary: Large Mughal congregational mosque opposite Agra Fort, commissioned by Jahanara Begum, daughter of Shah Jahan.
history: The Taj Mahal official nearby-attractions page describes the Jama Masjid as a major Mughal mosque opposite Agra Fort and notes its association with Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara Begum.
